_note: Cross-family blend (Slavic + Steppe): a Slavicized Turkic steppe people - the Tatar/Cossack stamp, horse-nomad hordes of grassland and taiga who took on a Slavic settled veneer. Backbone = Mongol-Turkic (steppe: phonology, the ovog hordes, the Khan ladder); overlay = Slavic (the stanitsa settlements, the Ataman/Voevoda host-leaders, forest-edge towns). clan = clanhold. Seeds/shifts Neutral or Chaotic. Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Mongol-Turkic/Slavic registers (allowed, catalog 5.3); DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon from both parents (Steppe primary, Slavic variant), never real gods.

phonology.palette: Mongol-Turkic backbone (vowel harmony; kh, gh, ch, sh, ng, q; -ai/-tai; agglutinative -chi/-khan) with a Slavic overlay (the sibilants, -ov/-ich patronymics, stanitsa/gorod settled register); theophoric on the Steppe morphs (Marakhai-, Tamendei-) with Slavic variants (Marakh-, Tulor-).
phonology.phonotactics: CV/CVC, no initial clusters; vowel harmony; the Slavic overlay adds -ov/-ich and heavier clusters in town-names.

morphology.patronymic_form: patronymic father + -in (steppe) or Slavic -ov/-ich among the settled; the ovog (clan); a deed- or animal-byname.
morphology.compounding_rule: [quality|animal](stem) + feature: Har-uul (black-mountain), Altan-gol (golden-river); the horde named for its khan; Slavic-overlay -stanitsa/-gorod for the settled holds.

title_ladder.government: clanhold (a horse-nomad horde with a Slavic settled veneer: the Khan and the ovog-clans, the Ataman host-leaders and the stanitsa garrisons; the khural raises the khan)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Mongol-Turkic backbone, ascending, with a Slavic overlay at the settled tiers. Noyan (noble) barony; Tarkhan (privileged border-lord) march, over a Slavic Kraina (frontier); Ataman (Cossack host-chief, overlay) county, over a Stanitsa; Voevoda (Slavic war-leader) duchy; Beki (great chief) principality; Khan (king) kingdom; Khagan (khan of khans), also hailed Velikii Khan, over the Yeke Ulus. (Rank titles are the real Mongol-Turkic/Slavic register, allowed.)

people_name_convention.order: personal + father's name (-in, steppe) or -ov/-ich (Slavic, among the settled); the ovog (clan); a deed/animal byname or the honor Baatar.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the horde-kin carry an ovog and steppe byname; the stanitsa-settled use Slavic -ov/-ich names.
people_name_convention.theophoric: names invoke the Eternal Sky and the war-powers + an element: Munke- (eternal), -baatar (hero), Tomor- (iron); the settled add Slavic Bog- (god) / -slav. e.g. Munke-baatar, Tulor-slav.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon (Steppe primary, from family_steppe theonym_set; Slavic variant, from family_slavic theonym_set), never real steppe/Slavic gods. Kypchan seeds/shifts Neutral or Chaotic; its stance follows its CURRENT alignment (see worship_by_alignment). The ovoo (sacred cairn) and the open sky are the steppe altars; the settled keep the Dedy (ancestral dead) and the kapishche-grove.
religion.the_one: Eterun (< Aeternus; Slavic variant Oterun) - the Eternal Sky; reviled as the cold sky-tyrant when Chaotic, acknowledged as the distant Heaven-Father when Neutral

sample_deity_renames.Maraxus: Marakhai (Slav. Marakh) - the war-fire, the raider; Chaotic power
sample_deity_renames.Gaiandus: Gajan (Slav. Goyan) - the enduring earth; Lawful power

worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: venerate the Chaotic powers (Marakhai the war-fire, Tamendei the storm, Lusantai the plunder-serpent), demonize the Lawful powers and the One (Eterun)
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: all powers ambivalent - somewhat honored, somewhat feared; foreground the Dedy (ancestral dead), the animal-spirits and the powers of place

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the demonized set (the Lawful powers + the One, when Chaotic) take dread epithets: Tulrius -> Tulai the Soft-Sun; Orlandus -> Orloch the Oath-Chain; Aeternus -> Eterun the Sky-Tyrant.
religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Ovoo (sacred cairn) of [power] on a high place, and among the settled the Kapishche (idol-grove): 'the Ovoo of Marakhai', 'the Kapishche of Tamendei'.
religion.saints_pattern: the great khans and hero-baatars become sky-riders among the storm; the settled honor the Dedy at the kurgan.

holy_symbol_motifs.Marakhai: a red horsetail war-standard (tug) beneath a black storm
holy_symbol_motifs.Tamendei: forked lightning over the open steppe
holy_symbol_motifs.Eterun: the open blue circle of the bare sky

banks_patterns.ships: river-craft of the great rivers and the horse-standards: 'the Black Tug', 'Storm of the Gol', 'the Wind-Eater' (a famed steed)
banks_patterns.military_units: the decimal host and the Cossack bands: the [khan] Tumen (10,000) / the [ataman] Sotnia (hundred): 'the Wolf Tumen', 'the Black Sotnia'
banks_patterns.taverns: the airag-tent and the stanitsa hall: 'the Khan's Airag-tent', 'the Red Stanitsa-Hall'
banks_patterns.dungeons_ruins: abandoned ordu-camps, burned stanitsas and kurgan barrow-tombs: 'the Kurgan of [khan]', 'the dead Stanitsa of [name]'
